title: Multi-GPU latency and unit-cost sweep across A10/L4/A100/H100
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run an end-to-end performance and cost sweep across our target GPU families (A10, L4, A100, H100) using a production-like traffic mix. Goals: (1) produce tokens/sec and p95 latency baselines for a mixed workload (assistant-style turns + short completions + embeddings), (2) quantify cost-per-1M-tokens under realistic batching and cache-warm scenarios, (3) add regression detection rules to CI/nightly runs and surface alerts for p95 drift or tokens/sec regressions. Deliverables: a metrics matrix, cost model, CI job config, and dashboards with thresholded alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline sweep completed for A10/L4/A100/H100 with cold and warm KV cache profiles
Results summarized in a machine-readable metrics matrix stored in S3 and linked from the ticket
Cost-per-1M-tokens calculated using standardized cloud hourly rates and occupancy assumptions
Regression detection algorithm integrated into nightly CI and documented in the runbook
Grafana dashboard and Slack alert channel configured; thresholds reviewed by SRE and Runtime owners
steps_taken: Defined synthetic traffic trace derived from 500k anonymized prod requests (70% assistant-like, 20% short completions, 10% embeddings)
Built harness that exercises sequence lengths [64, 256, 1024] with variable batching (single-request, 4, 16, continuous batching target) and KV cache states (cold, warm)
Implemented CI job 'perf/sweeps/multi-gpu' which provisions single-GPU instances for each family, runs 30-minute steady-state windows, and uploads metrics to s3://redwood-perf/matrix/2026-03
Captured tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, memory occupancy, and kernel-selection logs for each run
Prototype regression detection: EWMA on p95 with 14-day baseline and a confirmation window of 3 runs before firing a Slack alert
metrics_summary: Key baseline (mixed-workload, warm KV cache, continuous batching target=8): tokens/sec: A10=9.2k, L4=18.4k, A100=42.1k, H100=75.0k. p95 latency (ms): A10=240, L4=130, A100=58, H100=34. Cost-per-1M-tokens (USD, modeled): A10=$1.34, L4=$0.68, A100=$0.30, H100=$0.17. Observed trade-offs: A10 shows increased p95 variance at sequence=1024 under high concurrency; L4 is cost-efficient for short sequences; A100/H100 both scale well but H100 shows best tokens/sec per dollar in our occupancy assumptions.
notes_and_tradeoffs: We intentionally used a mixed workload (assistant-heavy) to reflect RLHF-style context churn which stresses KV cache behavior
Continuous batching improved tokens/sec by 10-25% on A100/H100 but increased p95 variance on A10 under high qps
Cost model assumes 70% occupancy for committed capacity; burst pricing and preemptible instances were excluded to keep comparisons conservative
Kernel selection logs indicate fallback to slower matmul kernels for certain int8 quantized checkpoints — follow-up: add targeted kernel A/B tests
Edge case: L4 showed occasional 5–10% throughput drops correlated with PCIe bandwidth saturation in multi-tenant hosts; flagged for infra investigation
regression_detection_design: Metric signals: primary=p95 latency, secondary=tokens/sec, tertiary=p99 for tail
Detection algorithm: EWMA baseline with sigma threshold + confirmation window (=3 runs) to avoid flapping
Multivariate signal: Hotelling T-squared used during initial analysis to detect correlated drift between p95 and tokens/sec
CI integration: nightly job stores metrics snapshot; diff algorithm compares latest snapshot vs 14-day baseline; failures create GitHub issue template and post to #perf-regressions
Runbook: explain isolation steps (re-run with cold cache, collect kernel logs, reproduce with single-sequence length)
next_steps: Automate upload of full kernel-selection traces to artifact storage and link to perf run for faster root-cause analysis
Add quantization sweep (fp16 vs int8) and model variant column to results_matrix
Coordinate with SRE to test L4 PCIe saturation hypothesis on dedicated hosts (ENG-34710)
Work with Console team to add cost-per-route breakdown to Redwood Console using this metrics matrix as initial mapping
